Done. T2 solved with a single execution of the plan.

**Deliverables**
- `out/T2/plan.yaml` — the BrainSurgery plan (no Python)
- `out/T2/model.safetensors` — 160 tensors, float32
- `out/T2/REPORT.md` — self-report

**Approach.** `concat` accepts sliced source references directly, so each head-bearing tensor is rebuilt from its surviving blocks in one step — no `split` and no per-piece cleanup. Since destinations must not already exist, each tensor goes: `concat` → scratch name, `delete` original, `move` scratch back onto the original name. Names and tensor count are preserved.

The layout is the actual work. Under Conv1D `[in, out]`, heads are **columns** of the fused `c_attn.weight` (three separate q/k/v blocks at `320:384`, `1088:1152`, `1856:1920` on dim 1) but **rows** of `c_proj.weight` (one block at `320:384` on dim 0). Slicing `c_proj` on the wrong axis would yield a plausible `[768, 704]` and garbage attention. Also avoided: `attn.bias` is the `[1,1,1024,1024]` causal mask, not a projection bias, so any `attn\..*bias` pattern would have swept it up.

**Checks.** The four required asserts, plus the same shape checks across all 12 layers, the untouched `c_proj.bias`/`attn.bias` shapes, 12-match counts, no surviving scratch tensors, and dtype — all before the write.

**Verification after the run** (separate plans, not the artifact): `diff` shows exactly 36 differing tensors and nothing missing on either side, with an `assert: equal` proving every other tensor bit-identical; 23 slice-level equality checks confirm each kept block matches its source block bit-exactly, plus a negative control that the columns at the old `320:384` seam no longer match — head 5 is genuinely removed, not truncated off the end.
